subject.title: fix: allow bailian provider in resolveThinkingProfile

question: Should OpenClaw accept treating custom configured `bailian` Qwen compat rows as reasoning-capable by default, or defer that behavior to Qwen/Coding Plan provider-owned support?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent support boundary affects provider/model behavior for existing custom configs and overlaps the broader open Coding Plan support issue.

options.title: Accept narrow custom-provider inference after cleanup
options.body: Land the generic configured-model Bailian inference only after removing the vLLM hook change, adding focused tests, and receiving changed-path real behavior proof.

options.title: Fold into Qwen/Coding Plan work
options.body: Ask contributors to handle Bailian reasoning through the canonical Qwen/Coding Plan provider and catalog path instead of adding a custom-provider inference special case here.

options.title: Defer broad Bailian reasoning
options.body: Keep current conservative behavior until model-by-model Alibaba proof establishes which Bailian/Coding Plan combinations should be enabled.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow custom-provider inference after cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the generic configured-model Bailian inference only after removing the vLLM hook change, adding focused tests, and receiving changed-path real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the adjacent Qwen thinking-format support and is already named in related review history as the routing owner for the provider-boundary decision.
